<issue>
Speed calculation produces division by zero error

#### Description

When adding missing speed data to GPX tracks, the speed calculation fails with a ZeroDivisionError. This happens when the time difference between consecutive points becomes zero.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import gpxpy

# Create a simple GPX with points that have the same timestamp
gpx_content = '''<?xml version="1.0"?>
<gpx version="1.1" creator="test">
  <trk>
    <trkseg>
      <trkpt lat="45.0" lon="0.0">
        <time>2023-01-01T12:00:00Z</time>
      </trkpt>
      <trkpt lat="45.001" lon="0.001">
        <time>2023-01-01T12:00:00Z</time>
      </trkpt>
      <trkpt lat="45.002" lon="0.002">
        <time>2023-01-01T12:00:01Z</time>
      </trkpt>
    </trkseg>
  </trk>
</gpx>'''

gpx = gpxpy.parse(gpx_content)
gpx.add_missing_speeds()  # This raises ZeroDivisionError
```

The error occurs because when two consecutive points have identical timestamps, the time difference becomes zero, leading to division by zero in the speed calculation formula.
